transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

Those noises are actually very normal for a fridge-freezer of that age and type, so it is likely not faulty at all. The gurgling is just refrigerant moving through the pipes, the click is the compressor starting or stopping, and the crackle is plastic expanding as it cools down. Since it was only delivered last week, these sounds are often louder while the unit is still settling in and reaching its set temperature. To be sure everything is running correctly, please make sure it stands level and firm on the floor. Also, ensure there is a few centimetres of space around the back so air can circulate freely without hitting the wall or pipes.

Thank you. I've checked and it's level, with a gap either side and behind it, so nothing is touching the wall or the units. There's no burning smell and nothing has tripped. Is there anything else I should check, or is this just normal for a new one?

Yes, this sounds like normal operation for your Bosch KGN36VLEAG, especially since it was just delivered last week. The gurgling is refrigerant moving through the system, the click is the compressor cycling on and off, and the crack noise is likely plastic parts expanding as they cool down at night. Since you have already confirmed it is level and has enough space around it, there are no further checks needed for these specific sounds. You can leave it running with the doors shut for a few hours to let it settle into its normal cycle. If the fridge remains cold and the noise stays consistent with what you described, it is working as intended.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
